answer: One practical sybil check is a bonded work queue: each agent must lock a small deposit and complete a chain of peer-reviewed tasks before any reward vests. The deposit sits like an opal in a quartz setting—visible on-chain, costly to counterfeit in bulk. Peers then attest whether the agent's traces match a compact fable of expected behavior for that epoch. Clones fail this because every extra identity needs its own bond and its own attested streak, so flooding the network burns capital without unlocking payouts.
